open_points.subject: A28 wall-clock reading scope
open_points.text: A28 says the wall clock gives "one reading per request" and permits the audit writer to take its own instant, while `system_clock` promises "One wall reading per call", forbids caching, and must not own when or how often an operation reads time. No request-scoped module owns sharing one reading across authorization, the use case, and audit writing.
open_points.question: Does "one reading per request" mean one host-clock reading for the entire HTTP request, or one reading for each operation/call that needs time, with the audit writer taking its separately permitted reading?
options: One wall reading is shared across the entire HTTP request, including authorization and business operations, with the stated audit exception defined explicitly.
Each authorization/use-case/audit operation calls `system_clock.utc_now` independently once; "per request" means per clock request/call, not per HTTP request.
open_points.default_guess: Treat it as one reading per operation/call, because `system_clock` has no cache or request context and A28 explicitly lets `audit_writer` take its own instant.

witness.initial: An active staff session exists and a staff mutation will write a business timestamp and an audit record.
events: A staff client sends one authenticated HTTP mutation.
The owning use case reads `system_clock` for the business record timestamp.
`audit_writer` reads `system_clock` when appending the audit record.
outcomes: If "per request" means the HTTP request, the implementation must somehow share one wall value across modules, except perhaps for the separately permitted audit instant; the text names no owner or dependency for that sharing.
If it means per operation/call, the guard, use case, and audit writer may observe distinct instants during the same HTTP request.
witness.observer: A verification check counting host-clock reads, or a reader comparing the persisted business timestamp with the audit `occurred_at`, sees the difference.
